title: Safety, privacy and responsible engineering
summary: Threat-model LLM and agent systems with the OWASP LLM and Agentic Top 10s, harden the web/API layer (authZ, tenant isolation, SSRF, secrets, supply chain), go deep on prompt injection and the design patterns that actually reduce it, automate red-teaming in CI, and cover PII, fairness, cards/licensing/governance and incident response.

units.title: Threat-modelling LLM applications with the OWASP LLM Top 10 (2025)
outcomes: You can draw a data-flow diagram with trust boundaries for an LLM/agent system.
You can map all 10 OWASP LLM risks to attack paths, controls and gaps in a risk register.

quiz.prompt: An example of LLM05 Improper Output Handling is…
options: rendering model output as HTML without sanitising it
quiz.explain: Model output is untrusted input to downstream systems (XSS, SQLi).

quiz.prompt: LLM10 Unbounded Consumption covers…
quiz.explain: Rate limits, quotas and budgets are the controls.

quiz.prompt: LLM07 System Prompt Leakage implies you should…
options: never put secrets or authorization logic in the system prompt
quiz.explain: Assume the system prompt will be extracted.

practice.title: Harden your FastAPI service
practice.brief: Add JWT auth, per-tenant row-level filtering (including vector-store metadata filters), secrets from env/secret manager (run gitleaks on the repo), rate limiting, and a URL-fetch tool with an SSRF allowlist that blocks private IPs and cloud metadata addresses.
practice.done_when: Tests prove: cross-tenant read → 403/empty; fetch of 169.254.169.254 and 127.0.0.1 → blocked; gitleaks reports 0 findings; rate limit returns 429.

quiz.prompt: BOLA (broken object-level authorization) means…
options: a user can access another user's object by changing an id
quiz.explain: Check ownership on every object access.

quiz.prompt: SSRF in an agent's fetch tool can expose…
options: internal services and cloud metadata endpoints
quiz.explain: The server fetches on the attacker's behalf.

quiz.prompt: Tenant isolation in RAG requires…
options: filtering retrieval by tenant/ACL before results reach the model
quiz.explain: The model can't un-see another tenant's chunk.

quiz.prompt: Why must authorization be enforced in the tool/back end, not in the prompt?
rubric: Prompts can be overridden by injection
Back-end checks are deterministic and auditable
Model never holds more privilege than the user

practice.title: Lock, audit, admit

quiz.prompt: Loading an untrusted pickle model file can…
quiz.explain: Pickle deserialisation runs code.

quiz.prompt: A lock file with hashes protects against…

quiz.prompt: Third-party skills with scripts should be…
options: reviewed and sandboxed like any code
quiz.explain: A skill is code plus instructions.

quiz.prompt: Describe your admission checklist for a new MCP server.
rubric: Source/maintainer and licence check
Pinned version + descriptor hash; re-review on change
Least-privilege scopes, sandbox/egress limits and logging

practice.title: 40-attack corpus
practice.brief: Build an adversarial corpus of 40 injections (direct, indirect via retrieved docs, via tool output, via image text, markdown-image exfiltration) and run it against your capstone. Report attack success rate per channel.
practice.done_when: attacks/ contains 40 cases with expected-safe behaviour; a report shows ASR per channel.

quiz.prompt: Indirect prompt injection arrives via…
options: content the agent reads (web pages, emails, docs, tool output)
quiz.explain: The attacker never talks to the model directly.

quiz.prompt: Markdown-image exfiltration works by…
options: encoding data in an image URL the client auto-fetches
quiz.explain: Rendering triggers a GET to the attacker.

quiz.prompt: Jailbreak vs prompt injection:
options: a jailbreak targets the model's safety policy; injection hijacks the application's instructions/data flow
quiz.explain: Different threat models, overlapping techniques.

quiz.prompt: Why can't injection be 'fully solved' by filtering inputs?
rubric: Natural language has no clean code/data boundary
Attackers adapt; filters are probabilistic
Design-level capability limits are needed

units.title: Design patterns that actually reduce injection risk
outcomes: You can re-architect a flow with dual-LLM, plan-then-execute or action-selector so untrusted content can't trigger side effects.
You can measure attack success and utility before/after a pattern.

learn.slice: Sections 3–4: the six patterns and case studies

covers: Action-selector, plan-then-execute, LLM map-reduce, dual LLM, code-then-execute, context-minimization
Trade-off between utility and provable resistance

practice.title: Re-architect one flow
practice.brief: Re-architect one capstone flow using dual-LLM or plan-then-execute so untrusted content can never choose a side-effecting tool. Re-run the M18.U04 corpus and report attack success rate before/after plus the utility drop on your normal eval set.
practice.done_when: Before/after ASR and task-success numbers in one table; an architecture diagram shows the quarantined LLM path.

quiz.prompt: In the dual-LLM pattern, the privileged LLM…
options: never sees raw untrusted content, only symbolic references
quiz.explain: A quarantined LLM handles untrusted text.

quiz.prompt: Least privilege for agents means…
options: each tool/credential gets the minimum scope for the task
quiz.explain: Limits blast radius.

quiz.prompt: These patterns trade off…
quiz.explain: Provable guarantees constrain what the agent can do.

quiz.prompt: Which pattern fits an email-summarising assistant that can also send mail, and why?
rubric: Picks a pattern (e.g. dual-LLM or plan-then-execute with user-confirmed sends)
Explains how untrusted email text is kept from choosing recipients/actions
States the utility cost

practice.title: Red-team gate in CI
practice.brief: Add a red-team suite to CI: injection, denied actions (the agent must refuse or be blocked), PII leakage and benign prompts. Gate merges on attack success ≤ threshold AND benign false-refusal rate ≤ threshold.
practice.done_when: A CI run fails on a deliberately weakened build and passes on the fixed one; thresholds documented with reasons.

quiz.prompt: Measuring only attack success is incomplete because…
options: over-blocking benign requests also harms users
quiz.explain: Track false refusals too.

quiz.prompt: A denied-action test asserts that…
options: a forbidden tool call is blocked by policy even if the model attempts it
quiz.explain: Tests the gate, not the model's manners.

quiz.prompt: Output validation includes…
options: schema checks, sanitisation and policy classifiers before output reaches users or systems
quiz.explain: Treat output as untrusted.

quiz.prompt: What is your regression threshold and why?
rubric: States numeric thresholds for ASR and false-refusal
Justifies from risk/harm and current baseline
Explains how flakiness/variance is handled (repeats, CI)

covers: Analyzer: NER + pattern recognisers + context words with confidence scores
Anonymizer operators: replace, redact, mask, hash, encrypt
Supported entities and languages; image redaction module

practice.title: Redact before export
practice.brief: Add PII detection/redaction (CNIC numbers, Pakistani phone numbers, emails) before logging and tracing. Add a custom recogniser for CNIC (#####-#######-#). Set a retention policy and a deletion endpoint; test with seeded PII.
practice.done_when: Tests: seeded CNIC/phone/email never appear in logs or exported traces; deletion endpoint removes a user's records; retention job documented.

quiz.prompt: Data minimisation means…
options: collect and keep only what the purpose needs
quiz.explain: Less data, less risk.

quiz.prompt: The safest place to redact PII for traces is…
quiz.explain: Redact at the trust boundary.

quiz.prompt: Pattern-based PII detection fails on…
quiz.explain: Combine patterns with NER/context and tests.

quiz.prompt: What PII might appear in an agent's tool outputs that you didn't expect?
rubric: Gives concrete examples (addresses in search results, names in tickets, IDs in documents)
Explains it bypasses input-side redaction
Proposes output-side redaction before logging/memory

practice.brief: Evaluate your M15 or M07 model (or an LLM classifier) across subgroups (language, region, gender if consented). Report metric gaps with bootstrap confidence intervals and one mitigation.

quiz.prompt: Demographic parity requires…
options: equal positive prediction rates across groups
quiz.explain: Independent of true labels.

quiz.prompt: Fairness criteria can…
options: conflict with each other, so the choice depends on context
quiz.explain: Impossibility results when base rates differ.

quiz.prompt: Small subgroup sizes require…
quiz.explain: Noise can look like bias.

quiz.prompt: Which fairness criterion fits a loan pre-screening assistant, and why?

quiz.prompt: A model card should state…
options: intended use, limitations and evaluation by slice
quiz.explain: Mitchell et al. 2019.

quiz.prompt: NIST AI RMF core functions are…
quiz.explain: Govern is cross-cutting.

quiz.prompt: 'Open weights' always means unrestricted commercial use:
quiz.explain: Many licences have use or scale restrictions.

practice.title: Tabletop drill
practice.brief: Write an incident runbook (detect → contain/kill switch → notify → fix → postmortem) and run a tabletop drill of 'agent leaked another tenant's data'. Add an abstain/escalate-to-human path for low confidence. Fix 3 accessibility issues (WCAG 2.2 A/AA) in your UI.
practice.done_when: RUNBOOK.md, a written blameless postmortem of the drill, a test for the escalate path, and 3 accessibility fixes referenced to WCAG success criteria.

quiz.prompt: A blameless postmortem focuses on…
options: systemic causes and fixes, not individual blame
quiz.explain: Blame suppresses reporting.

quiz.prompt: Escalating to a human is appropriate when…
options: confidence is low or the action is high-impact/irreversible
quiz.explain: Match autonomy to risk.

quiz.prompt: A risk register should be…
options: versioned and reviewed, with owner, likelihood/impact and mitigation
quiz.explain: It is a living artifact.

quiz.prompt: What triggers your kill switch automatically?
rubric: Names concrete signals (budget exceeded, denied-action spike, anomalous egress, error rate)
Thresholds stated
Says what the switch does and who is notified

capstone.title: Secure the agent
capstone.brief: Take your M12 capstone and deliver: a threat model (DFD + OWASP LLM and Agentic mapping), a risk register, a red-team CI suite with before/after metrics, one architectural injection defense, a PII redaction pipeline, model/system/dataset cards, and an incident runbook plus a drill write-up.

levels: 1: list of risks without data flow
3: all trust boundaries; every OWASP LLM + Agentic risk addressed or justified N/A
3: pattern (dual-LLM/plan-then-execute/least privilege) proven by before/after tests
3: red-team + denied-action + benign false-refusal metrics gating CI
3: redaction verified on seeded PII; retention/deletion; licences and cards complete
3: runbook, tested kill switch, blameless postmortem of the drill
